مُجَالِحٌ i. q. مُكَابِرٌ [Contending with another for superiority in greatness; &c.: see its verb, 3]. (S.) ―
-b2- The lion. (K.) ―
-b3- A she-camel that yields
milk abundantly in winter: (S, K:) or that crops the twigs of the dry trees in winter, in a year of drought, and becomes fat upon them, and so preserves her milk: (IAar, TA:) pl. ↓ مَجَالِيحُ : (S, K:) or this is pl. of مُجَالِحٌ and ↓ مِجْلَاحٌ as epithets applied to a palm-tree and a she-camel that cares not for the want of rain. (AHn, TA.) And مُجَالَحَةٌ A she-camel that eats the سَمُر and عُرْفُط, whether they have leaves upon them or not. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
